anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves all four facts in the intended direction and keeps nothing that Before held and After lost. Before never named the stuck exits: A and C rendered a recommended ordinary `wait - run one bounded CI watch` row and a numeric `show evidence` row, B merely 'paused' with a stop recommendation rather than a named `stuck - run record unreadable` exit, and Before also discarded the retained course and recounted the budget against the configured 5 instead of the record's cap. After names each exit verbatim (`stuck - merge state unknown`, `stuck - run record unreadable`, `GitHub reports BLOCKED, no local repair applies`), preserves usage 1/10 and 2/10 unchanged, performs exactly one re-poll in A and none in C, refuses to recreate counters or search another record in B, treats reviewDecision only as a locator with no rule or approval demand in C, and renders a uniform obstacle menu with stop recommended last, evidence relegated to a hint, and no wait row or automatic merge. The one thing worth tightening is B's `Not offered` line, which mentions the course rows and merge but could also spell out that extension is unavailable because no record exists to extend; otherwise the After wording delivers the Change without regressing any fact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and gains f1 and f4: in A it performs the single re-poll, states that exit check selects the merge-state obstacle before any watch or repair, and leaves both counters at 1/10 and 2/10, while all three checkpoints now render the shared obstacle template with deliver/assess rows (or stop alone in B), stop recommended and last, show evidence demoted to a hint, and no ordinary wait row or merge. The one soft spot is labeling: A's narration says it exits on the merge-state obstacle, but the rendered verdict still reads 'fixable - merge state unknown' rather than 'stuck - merge state unknown' (B does say 'stuck - run record unreadable' explicitly), so a reader has to infer the stuck exit from the obstacle menu; echoing the exact exit label in A's verdict line (and in C, 'GitHub reports BLOCKED, no local repair applies') would make f1/f3 unambiguous without altering the menu shape. Also B's 'Delivers' line was reworded to 'stated intent', which is fine for an unvalidated continuation but worth keeping deliberate so the brief is not read as a new assessment.
